title: Supply-chain dependency review & evidence matrix (RBAC-aware) - Jul 2024
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines an evidence matrix and automated runbook for integrating dependency scanner output with RBAC v2 context, SIEM exports, and our vulnerability remediation workflow. Goal: reduce time-to-evidence and ensure every remediation has auditable verification artifacts tied to a SIEM event and the audit log snapshots required for compliance reviews.

Scope:
- OSS and internal dependency findings surfaced by licensed scanners (Snyk, Dependabot, Trivy) and our SBOM ingestion pipeline.
- Mapping of scanner artifacts to Jira issues, required evidence attachments, SIEM field mappings, and RBAC ownership checks.
- Patch SLA guidance for severity tiers and an automated tracker for remediation progress.

Executive summary (most recent scanner run: 2025-02-10 ingest):
- Total distinct findings (after dedupe across scanners): 183
- By severity: Critical: 4, High: 28, Medium: 64, Low: 87
- Top components (by hit count): openssl (CVE-2024-XXXXX) 12, protobuf 9, fastjson 7
- Estimated actionable backlog (requires human triage due to RBAC ownership unresolved): 42

Patch SLAs (recommended operational targets):
- Critical: 72 hours (ticket created automatically; oncall escalation at 24h)
- High: 7 days (owner assignment within 48h)
- Medium: 30 days
- Low: 90 days
Notes: SLAs assume CI build and smoke test can be completed within the window; exceptions allowed with documented compensating controls.

Remediation tracking & evidence requirements (per-ticket template):
Required evidence attachments before marking 'resolved':
1) Patch artifact or dependency bump PR link (GitHub PR URL).
2) CI build log snippet showing successful rebuild (text or log link).
3) Verification scan output (scanner JSON snippet showing the finding no longer present).
4) Audit log export showing the deployment/merge event (correlation_id present).
5) SIEM event id(s) that show the detection and follow-up (forwarder-generated event id).
Naming convention for evidence folder: <JIRA-ID>_<component>_<CVE>_<YYYYMMDD> (example: JIRA-SEC-342_openssl_CVE-2024-XXXXX_20250212)

Automated pipeline (high-level):
1) Scanner output ingestion (daily cron) -> normalize to canonical finding schema
2) Ownership resolution: query RBAC v2 owner map service for resource/component owners
3) Create or update Jira ticket using templated body; include normalized finding and suggested patch PR (if auto-fix available)
4) Trigger Slack alert to owner channel with interactive actions (create PR, acknowledge, reassign)
5) When PR is opened and CI passes, evidence automation picks up artifacts and attaches to Jira; also emits SIEM event for compliance tracing
6) Post-remediation verification: run targeted scanner (suppress duplicates) and append verification output to ticket and evidence store

Canonical finding schema (fields we store in vuln index):
- finding_id (unique-uid)
- scanner (snyk|dependabot|trivy|custom)
- component (group:artifact or package name)
- version
- cve (optional)
- severity (critical|high|medium|low)
- first_seen (ISO8601)
- last_seen (ISO8601)
- owner (team alias resolved via RBAC v2)
- suggested_fix (text/PR link)
- evidence_links (list of artifact urls)
- status (new|triaged|in_progress|resolved|wontfix)

Sample scanner snippet (normalized) - show as plain text to guide implementers:
{ finding_id: "f-20250209-001", scanner: "trivy", component: "openssl", version: "1.1.1k", cve: "CVE-2024-XXXXX", severity: "high", first_seen: "2025-02-09T03:12:00Z" }

RBAC v2 integration notes:
- Before creating an auto-assigned ticket, query RBAC owner service: GET /rbac/v2/component-owners?component=openssl. If no owner returned, mark ticket 'owner_needed' and route to sec-ops triage rotation.
- Audit logs must capture: grant/revoke events, role_id, actor_email, request_context, correlation_id, effective_permissions. These fields are required in the audit export attached to remediation evidence when the fix touches role mappings or access changes.
- For dependencies that are internal packages, include package ACL snapshot (from package registry) as an evidence artifact.

SIEM export mapping (fields we push into SIEM for each lifecycle transition):
- event_time (ISO8601)
- finding_id
- component
- cve
- severity
- action (detected|ticket_created|pr_opened|ci_passed|verification_passed|evidence_attached)
- actor (github_user|jira_user|service_account)
- correlation_id (UUID linking scanner -> jira -> ci -> deploy)
- owner_team
- sbom_snapshot_id

Evidence automation runbook (detailed steps for automation engineer):
1) Normalize scanner outputs to canonical schema (script: tools/normalize_scans.py).
2) Resolve owners via RBAC v2; fallback to tag-based owner lookup (package.json > security.owner).
3) Use Jira API to create issue with fields: summary, component, cve, severity, suggested_fix, owner_team, evidence_folder. Attach raw scanner JSON (redact PII).
4) Spawn GitHub branch suggestion bot (if auto-fix available) and post suggested PR link to Jira.
5) On PR merge, CI posts webhook to automation service; automation collects build log URL, constructs audit export (extract correlation_id from commit message), and posts to Jira as attachment.
6) Automation forwards a structured event to SIEM via our log-forwarder endpoint (/logs/vuln-lifecycle) including correlation_id.
7) Mark Jira status to 'verification in progress' and run targeted verify scanner; attach verification JSON to Jira and signal 'resolved' on success.

Verification acceptance criteria (for automated close):
- Verification scan report shows finding_id absent or status remediated; AND
- CI build for PR referenced in ticket completed within last 7 days; AND
- Evidence artifacts (at least 3 of 5 required) are present and accessible in evidence storage; AND
- SIEM event for 'verification_passed' present with matching correlation_id.

Operational considerations / gotchas observed in pilots:
- Multiple scanners produce different identifiers for the same underlying vuln. Must dedupe on component+version+CVE where available.
- Some internal packages lack owner metadata in RBAC store; add a 'package_owner' tag to registry entries to improve lookup success.
- RBAC v2 permission changes can create noise when deployment automation updates role bindings; correlate by correlation_id to avoid false reopenings.

Open action items and owners:
- [ ] Implement normalized scanner ingestion lambda (owner: Elliot Zhang) - ETA 2025-03-01
- [ ] Add package_owner field to internal registry (owner: Priya Nair) - ETA 2025-03-15
- [ ] Wire SIEM forwarder to vuln-lifecycle topic and validate field mapping (owner: Marco Gutierrez) - ETA 2025-02-28
- [ ] Draft playbook for auditor review demonstrating evidence chain for 3 historical incidents (owner: Samira Lopez) - ETA 2025-03-10

Appendix A: Example ticket template (Jira body):
Summary: [<component>] <short description> - <CVE>
Description:
- Finding ID: {{finding_id}}
- Component: {{component}}
- Version: {{version}}
- CVE: {{cve}}
- Severity: {{severity}}
- First seen: {{first_seen}}
- Suggested fix: {{suggested_fix}}
- Owner team (RBAC v2 resolved): {{owner_team}}
- Evidence folder: {{evidence_folder}}
Checklist:
- [ ] Assign owner
- [ ] Open PR / patch
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Attach verification scan output
- [ ] Attach audit export / SIEM id

Appendix B: Quick reference - SIEM event example (JSON payload we send):
{ "event_time": "2025-02-10T14:32:00Z", "finding_id": "f-20250209-001", "component": "openssl", "cve": "CVE-2024-XXXXX", "severity": "high", "action": "ticket_created", "actor": "automation_bot", "correlation_id": "c-9f8b7a6e" }

If there are questions on mapping or we need a shortened SLA for specific customers/tenants (Dedicated/Private), call out the exceptions in the Jira ticket and tag the ticket with 'sla-exception'.

Document history:
- 2024-07-16 initial draft (Samira Lopez)
- 2024-08-22 pilot notes added (Elliot Zhang)
- 2025-02-14 RBAC v2 integration and SIEM mapping updated (Samira Lopez)

End of document.
